groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–2 题
groups.material: African leaders plan to turn the continent into a continent without borders. They will introduce a single passport policy, allowing free movement between countries. The idea from the African Union has been modeled on the EU Schengen free movement deal. Europe has abolished many internal borders. This enables visa-free movement across the continent. Currently, 13 African countries have visa-free deals in place with each other. These allow citizens to visit another country without a visa. Some countries offer visas on arrival. In contrast, Americans are able to travel to 20 of the continent's countries without a visa, or secure a visa on arrival. The African Union, which represents 54 states, wants to abolish the requirement of a visa for Africans visiting other African countries. It also wants to establish a free trade deal across the continent in the near future, as trade within the African continent costs more than any other region.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 3–4 题
groups.material: Researchers in Iceland found a new way of tackling climate change by pumping carbon dioxide underground and turning it into stone. Other carbon capture and storage methods store carbon dioxide as a gas. But problems include a high cost and concern about leaks. This new method of burying carbon dioxide and turning it into stone is cheaper and more secure, the Guardian reports. To turn carbon dioxide into stone, researchers with the CarbFix project pumped the gas into volcanic rock and sped up the natural process, in which the volcanic rock reacts with gas and forms carbon minerals. The gas turned into solid in just two years, much faster than the hundreds or thousands of years researchers had predicted. The research took place at Iceland's Hellisheidi power plant. Already, the project in Iceland has been increased in scale to bury 10,000 tons of carbon dioxide each year. One potential difficulty is that for each ton of carbon dioxide buried, the technique requires 25 tons of water. However, the lead researcher said sea water could be used.

groups.title: Section A · 第 3 篇 · 5–7 题
groups.material:
People in France are keeping away from the narrow French stick loaf in favour of healthier, cheaper options, a millers' association has said. The National Association of French Millers says bread consumption is on the decline, with French people eating nine grams less than in the previous year. The association is concerned about the effects this trend will have on their trade and suggests three reasons why it is happening.
Firstly, the association cited changing diets, in particular, the switch to those low in calories, as a factor in the reduction of bread consumption. This could explain why the difference in consumption between genders is so big. Nowadays, men eat an approximate average of 140 grams of bread daily, whereas women eat 80 to 90 grams. The second reason they say is lifestyle changes in the country, with people dedicating less time to breakfast when bread would traditionally be eaten with butter and jam. Finally, the rising cost of bread is considered to be a factor, with the price of a French stick loaf increasing by nearly 25% in the last 10 years.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 8–11 题
groups.material:
W: Next, please.
M: Yes, I'd like to book two train tickets to London tomorrow morning, please.
W: Okay. What time would you like to go?
M: Well, after the rush hour, I think. We'd like to avoid the crowds if possible. So, probably sometime around 10 o'clock.
W: No problem. Just give me a minute. There's one here at 9:47, then one at 10:12, and then a third at 10:26.
M: The one at 10:12 sounds good.
W: All right. Would you like to sit in first or second class?
M: Second class is fine. Thanks. Is there any chance we could have a window seat for one of those?
W: No problem. And I've booked those seats next to each other for you. The total price is 36 pounds, 50 cents. Is there anything else?
M: Yes, actually, we'll be taking our bicycles with us. What is the arrangement for that? And will it cost extra?
W: It's no extra cost. The price will be the same. All you need to do is wait at the far end of the platform. When the train arrives, tell the train guard where you're going, and he will help you secure the bicycles in the last carriage and give you a ticket. Then you can walk down through the train to your carriage and take your seats. When you arrive in London, hand the ticket to the guard and he will return the bicycles to you.
M: Thank you for the information. That's very helpful.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
M: Good morning. Our guest today is Karen Brook. Karen is the managing director of Cube Movie Theater, located on Underhill Road. Thank you for coming, Karen.
W: Thank you for having me.
M: So, tell us about your cinema—Cube Movie Theater.
W: Sure. Cube Movie Theater has been around now for 11 years. It's located in what used to be a hat factory.
M: Oh, really?
W: Yeah. There used to be many hat factories in Britain until around the 1950s, but fashion changed and most people stopped wearing hats. So practically all of those factories had to close down. This one, in particular, was closed for 47 years before we transformed it into a movie theater.
M: I see. I hear there's something else that makes your theater special. What is it that sets you apart from other theaters?
W: We are the only movie theater in the whole country that only shows foreign movies.
M: Is there enough demand for that? I would have thought that in London, most people don't speak foreign languages.
W: Sure, there's enough demand. The fact that we have been open and in business for all these years proves it. London is a very large and international city. There are lots of people interested in watching such movies. Furthermore, I might add, all movies come with English text at the bottom of the screen. So even if you don't understand what the actors say, you can still read it.
M: Of course. What movie are you showing right now?
W: This week we're showing a musical from Pakistan. It's very popular.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
Love them or hate them, smartphones have become an integral part of our daily lives. But should they be left outside the classroom?
Nick Gibb, Minister for School Standards in England, believes schools should ban their pupils from bringing in smartphones.
Astrid Natley, a secondary school math teacher, incorporates phones into her classroom. "My school doesn't have money for tablets," she says. "When students use their phones for research, they learn they have a powerful tool in their hands. If we stop children using phones, we're rejecting something they care about."
Meanwhile, Helen Lockhart, a registered nurse working for community education, supports a complete ban. "I'm banned from mobile use at work, and my phone must be handed in. If I'm caught with it in my pocket, I will be subject to disciplinary procedure, which will impact on my career. We need to teach children how to behave like the professionals they are striving to become."
Richard Stone, an English teacher, thinks there should be a clear separation between school and home. "Students should do things differently in the two environments. Children are getting more than enough screen time in their lives without the need to bring their phone into the classroom. The internet is too easy and too unreliable a research tool, so let's leave phones and laptops at home, and show them a different world in their lessons—one of books and pens," he says.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
Kate, a six-year-old girl, helped her brother wash windows to get a reward promised by her mother, a purple doll that she wanted. She watched her mother order the doll online. The next day Kate asked if she could check the shipping status, so her mom clicked on the web page and then walked out of the room. Kate saw that her doll would be arriving the next afternoon, but then she noticed something else, suggestions about other dolls and toys she could order. 15 minutes and a few clicks later, with more than $350 worth of dolls in her cart, Kate placed the order and ran off to play.
The next day, while checking on another online order, her mother noticed a long list of dolls on the way. She was able to cancel two of them, but it was too late to cancel the rest. She told her daughter that they were going to be returned. When the packages arrived, Kate wanted to open them, but her parents said no. Instead of sending back the dolls, her father suggested giving them to the local children's hospital. So the next week, Kate's family loaded up their car and took all the dolls to the playroom at the children's hospital. Kate was depressed at first, but then she sat with some girl patients and they opened up all the boxes together, laughing and playing. She had a lot of fun and learned a really good lesson.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Can the date you were born affect how successful your life is? According to recent research done in Australia, the answer is yes. The researchers found that the time when a person starts school has an enduring impact on their lives. Those who are relatively old, compared to their classmates, have certain advantages over them. Previous research has found older students achieve better results. They are also more likely to attend university and become professional athletes, chief executives and even important politicians. But the Australian researchers wanted to discover what was driving these differences. They suspected older, more mature students obtained more self-confidence than their peers because they achieved better grades.
To test this out, they conducted two studies. One was with high school students and the other with more than a thousand Australian adults, age between 24 and 60 years old. In the first study more than 600 high school students were surveyed about their tendency to take risks and feel confident. In the second study, those born on both sides of the cutoff date for starting school were asked to complete online math questions and rate their performance. They were also asked about the risks they took while riding bicycles and managing their finances. The researchers found that older students displayed greater risk-taking tendencies. While risk-taking can be considered a negative attribute, it's also a characteristic of successful people, including athletes, political leaders and entrepreneurs.

questions.prompt: What is the news report mainly about?
options: A proposed policy allowing Africans to travel in Africa without a visa.
An agreement among 13 African countries to set up a free-trade zone.
A plan to invite all African countries to join the African Union.
An important initiative to permit tourists to visit Africa without a visa.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the news report mainly about? 

 【翻译】 这则新闻报道主要是关于什么的? 
 A)  一项允许非洲人在非洲境内免签旅行的拟议政策。 
 B)  13个非洲国家之间建立自由贸易区的协议。 
 C)  一项邀请所有非洲国家加入非洲联盟的计划。 
 D)  一项允许游客免签访问非洲的重要倡议。 

 【答案】 A （主旨题） A proposed policy allowing Africans to travel in Africa without a visa. 
 【定位】 P1 African leaders plan to turn the continent into a continent without borders. They will introduce a single passport policy, allowing free movement between countries. 
 非洲各国领导人计划把整个非洲大陆变成一个没有边界的大陆。他们将推出统一护照政策，允许各国之间自由通行。 

 【信号】 开头点题即主旨 。新闻类听力的导语句几乎就是主旨句。African leaders plan to turn the continent into a continent without borders. 这一句开门见山讲"非洲领导人要让整个非洲免边界（即免签）"，紧接着 They will introduce a single passport policy, allowing free movement between countries. 直接落到具体政策上——"政策+对象"全在这里。 

 【替换】 turn the continent into a continent without borders ↔ travel in Africa without a visa "无边界"="免签通行" 
 allowing free movement between countries ↔ Africans to travel in Africa free movement=travel 
 The African Union, which represents 54 states, wants to abolish the requirement of a visa for Africans visiting other African countries. ↔ A proposed policy allowing Africans to travel in Africa without a visa. 原文反复点 Africans+visa 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 盗用了录音 Currently, 13 African countries have visa-free deals in place with each other. 里的 13 African countries 这个数字原词，但原文说的是"目前已有 13 国互相免签"，根本不是"13 国设立自贸区"——自贸区在原文里是另一桩"未来要做的事"，不限于 13 国。  借用原文：Currently, 13 African countries have visa-free deals in place with each other. 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 盗用了原文 The African Union, which represents 54 states（非盟代表 54 个国家）中的 African Union 这一专名，制造"听到非盟就想选"的诱惑；但原文谈的是非盟"代表"54 国并推动免签自贸，根本没说要"邀请各国加入非盟"——加入与否不是本新闻的话题。  借用原文：The African Union, which represents 54 states 

 D) 张冠李戴 D 用 tourists 替换了原文里的 Africans——原文 Americans are able to travel to 20 of the continent's countries without a visa 是在拿"美国人（外来游客的代表）现状"与"非洲人现状"作对照，目的恰恰是说"非洲人反而不如外人方便、所以才要改"。把主体从"非洲人"偷换到"游客"，正好与新闻核心相反。  借用原文：Americans are able to travel to 20 of the continent's countries without a visa

questions.prompt: What benefit will a free trade deal bring to African economy?
options: It will attract more investments from all over the world.
It will help many African countries reduce trade deficits.
It will reduce the cost of trade between African countries.
It will allow Africans to play a bigger role in world trade.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What benefit will a free trade deal bring to African economy? 

 【翻译】 自由贸易协议将为非洲经济带来什么好处? 
 A)  它将吸引来自世界各地的更多投资。 
 B)  它将帮助许多非洲国家减少贸易逆差。 
 C)  它将降低非洲国家之间的贸易成本。 
 D)  它将使非洲人在世界贸易中发挥更大作用。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It will reduce the cost of trade between African countries. 
 【定位】 P1 It also wants to establish a free trade deal across the continent in the near future, as trade within the African continent costs more than any other region. 
 （非盟）还希望在不久的将来在整个非洲大陆建立自由贸易协定，因为目前非洲大陆内部的贸易成本比其他任何地区都要高。 

 【信号】 as 引出原因即落点 。答案句里出现因果信号词 as trade within the African continent costs more than any other region——as 在这里是"因为"。"自贸要解决的问题=非洲内部贸易最贵"，反过来推就是"自贸的好处=降低非洲内部贸易成本"。这就是听力"信号词后是落点"的典型用法。 

 【替换】 trade within the African continent costs more than any other region ↔ reduce the cost of trade between African countries 因果对调＋反义改写 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 录音通篇没提到 investment / invest 任何形式的词。A 听起来"很正确"是因为它符合考生对"自贸好处"的常识联想，但题目问的是录音里给出的好处，不是考生想到的好处。 
 B) 偷换概念 B 用 trade deficits（贸易逆差）替换了原文真正说的 trade costs（贸易成本）。"贸易成本"和"贸易逆差"是两个完全不同的经济概念——前者是"做生意要花多少钱"，后者是"进口比出口多多少"。选项利用了 trade 这个原词来诱选。  借用原文：trade within the African continent costs more than any other region 

 D) 过度推断 D 说的 a bigger role in world trade（在世界贸易中扮演更大角色）把范围从"非洲内部"扩到了"全世界"。原文里 free trade deal 限定的范围是 across the continent（在整个非洲大陆），目标是降低非洲国家之间的贸易成本，并未谈到非洲在世界贸易里的地位变化。  借用原文：establish a free trade deal across the continent

questions.prompt: What new method has been developed to help fight climate change?
options: Cooling down volcanic rock with sea water.
Storing carbon dioxide underground as a gas.
Capturing carbon dioxide and burying it under the sea.
Pumping carbon dioxide underground to form stone.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What new method has been developed to help fight climate change? 

 【翻译】 已经开发出什么新方法来帮助对抗气候变化？ 
 A)  用海水冷却火山岩。 
 B)  以气体形式将二氧化碳储存在地下。 
 C)  捕获二氧化碳并将其埋在海底。 
 D)  将二氧化碳泵入地下使其形成石头。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Pumping carbon dioxide underground to form stone. 
 【定位】 P1 Researchers in Iceland found a new way of tackling climate change by pumping carbon dioxide underground and turning it into stone. 
 冰岛的研究人员发现了一种应对气候变化的新方法：把二氧化碳泵入地下，将其变成石头。 

 【信号】 首句点题信号 a new way 。Researchers in Iceland found a new way of tackling climate change 中的 found a new way 与题干 new method 形成同义对接，是新闻典型的开门见山首句点题，这一句直接承载新方法是什么的答案。 

 【替换】 pumping carbon dioxide underground ↔ Pumping carbon dioxide underground 原词同形复现 
 turning it into stone ↔ to form stone turn into = form 的动词同义替换 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项把录音里两处出现的 volcanic rock 与 sea water 拼成 cooling down volcanic rock with sea water，但录音从未说过冷却火山岩这件事，cooling 是凭空造的动作。  借用原文：pumped the gas into volcanic rock 

 B) 张冠李戴 录音原文 Other carbon capture and storage methods store carbon dioxide as a gas. 明确说把二氧化碳以气体形式储存是其他/已有方法，本则新闻要讲的恰恰是与之对照的新方法；选项 B 把旧方法当成新方法的答案，是典型张冠李戴。  借用原文：Other carbon capture and storage methods store carbon dioxide as a gas. 

 C) 偷换概念 录音说的是 burying carbon dioxide and turning it into stone，埋的地方是地下（underground / volcanic rock），但选项 C 写成 burying it under the sea，把地点偷换成海底；只是单词长得像，意思完全偏。  借用原文：burying carbon dioxide and turning it into stone

questions.prompt: What is a potential difficulty in applying the new technique?
options: Lack of burying ground.
Long time for processing.
High consumption of water.
Enormous cost of energy.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is a potential difficulty in applying the new technique? 

 【翻译】 应用这项新技术的潜在困难是什么？ 
 A)  缺乏掩埋场地。 
 B)  处理时间长。 
 C)  水消耗量大。 
 D)  能源成本巨大。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） High consumption of water. 
 【定位】 P1 One potential difficulty is that for each ton of carbon dioxide buried, the technique requires 25 tons of water. 
 一个潜在的困难是，每埋藏一吨二氧化碳，这项技术需要 25 吨水。 

 【信号】 题干原词信号 One potential difficulty 。One potential difficulty is that 与题干 potential difficulty 用词几乎完全一致，是录音替我们点出的答案句信号词；这是新闻收尾段最常见的转折/补充结构，信号词后那一句就是承载答案的句子。 

 【替换】 requires 25 tons of water ↔ High consumption of water 数量级 → 程度词，动词 → 名词化 
 for each ton of carbon dioxide buried, the technique requires 25 tons of water ↔ High consumption of water 1∶25 比例支撑 High 这一判断 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 录音并未提到埋藏地点不够这件事，反而提到 the project in Iceland has been increased in scale to bury 10,000 tons of carbon dioxide each year，说明埋藏规模在扩大，不是缺地的问题；选项 A 属于无中生有。 
 B) 与原文相反 录音说的是 The gas turned into solid in just two years, much faster than the hundreds or thousands of years researchers had predicted.，明确强调这项技术比预期快得多，并不是耗时长；选项 B 取了 hundreds of years 这一原词却反了方向。  借用原文：The gas turned into solid in just two years, much faster than the hundreds or thousands of years researchers had predicted. 

 D) 原词陷阱 录音里的 Other carbon capture and storage methods store carbon dioxide as a gas. But problems include a high cost and concern about leaks. 中的 high cost 是描述其他/旧方法的问题，且讲的是费用而非 energy；选项 D 把 cost 与 energy 拼到一起，既张冠李戴（说的是旧方法）、又偷换概念（cost ≠ energy）。  借用原文：problems include a high cost and concern about leaks

questions.prompt: What does the news report say about French people's bread consumption?
options: It varies with the seasons.
It has been on the decline.
It has caused nationwide concern.
It is ninety grams daily on average.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the news report say about French people's bread consumption? 

 【翻译】 新闻报道关于法国人面包消费量说了什么? 
 A)  它随季节变化。 
 B)  它一直在下降。 
 C)  它引起了全国关注。 
 D)  平均每天九十克。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It has been on the decline. 
 【定位】 P1 The National Association of French Millers says bread consumption is on the decline, with French people eating nine grams less than in the previous year. 
 法国全国磨坊主协会表示，面包消费正在下滑，法国人比前一年少吃了 9 克。 

 【信号】 权威主体+趋势动词直陈 。The National Association of French Millers says bread consumption is on the decline 一句里，权威主体 says 引出对消费状况的直接断言，is on the decline 是清晰的趋势判定信号，是本题事实陈述题的典型答案句标志。 

 【替换】 bread consumption is on the decline ↔ It has been on the decline. 几乎原词直接对应 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 It varies with the seasons. 在录音里找不到任何 season/seasonal/winter/summer 之类的踪迹，属于完全凭空捏造的方向。 
 C) 录音里说 The association is concerned about the effects this trend will have on their trade，关注者是行业协会、关注对象是他们的生意，选项 nationwide concern 把范围扩大到了'全国关注'，是典型的范围/程度放大。  借用原文：The association is concerned about the effects this trend will have on their trade 

 D) 原词陷阱 录音里的 90 grams 出现在 women eat 80 to 90 grams，特指女性消费区间的上限，不是全体法国人的日均量；选项 It is ninety grams daily on average. 盗用了原文中的 90 grams 这个原词，却安到了'整体平均'头上，是典型原词陷阱。  借用原文：women eat 80 to 90 grams

questions.prompt: What do we learn about French women from their port?
options: They emphasize food variety.
They prefer French stick loaves.
They do more cooking than men.
They favor diets lower in calories.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about French women from their port? 

 【翻译】 从报告中我们对法国女性了解到什么? 
 A)  她们强调食物多样性。 
 B)  她们更喜欢法式长棍面包。 
 C)  她们比男性做更多的烹饪。 
 D)  她们偏爱低热量饮食。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They favor diets lower in calories. 
 【定位】 P2 Firstly, the association cited changing diets, in particular, the switch to those low in calories, as a factor in the reduction of bread consumption. This could explain why the difference in consumption between genders is so big. Nowadays, men eat an approximate average of 140 grams of bread daily, whereas women eat 80 to 90 grams. 
 首先，协会指出饮食结构的变化、特别是转向低卡饮食，是面包消费下降的一个原因。这或许能解释为什么男女之间的消费差距如此之大。如今男性日均吃约 140 克面包，而女性只吃 80 到 90 克。 

 【信号】 因果链 explain why+男女对比 。the switch to those low in calories 与 This could explain why the difference in consumption between genders is so big 通过 explain why 把低卡饮食与男女消费差异连成因果链，男性 140g/女性 80–90g 的对比正好印证女性更倾向低卡，这条因果链就是本题的答案信号。 

 【替换】 the switch to those low in calories ↔ favor diets lower in calories the switch to=favor 的同义改写 
 women eat 80 to 90 grams ↔ favor diets lower in calories 对比数据印证偏好 

 【排除】 A) They emphasize food variety. 在录音里找不到 variety/different kinds 之类的对应表达，属于无中生有。 
 B) 原词陷阱 录音 People in France are keeping away from the narrow French stick loaf 明确说法国人是'远离'法棍，而 They prefer French stick loaves. 偷换为'偏爱'，方向正好相反，且盗用了 French stick loaves 这一原词制造熟悉感。  借用原文：People in France are keeping away from the narrow French stick loaf 

 C) 偷换概念 They do more cooking than men. 在录音里完全没有 cook/cooking 的对应词，且男女对比的对象始终是'吃多少面包'而非'谁下厨'，属于编造对比维度。

questions.prompt: What is said about lifestyle changes of the French people?
options: They bake more bread at home.
They spend less time eating breakfast.
They eat more fruit than they used to.
They put jam instead of butter on bread.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is said about lifestyle changes of the French people? 

 【翻译】 关于法国人的生活方式变化说了什么? 
 A)  他们在家烤更多面包。 
 B)  他们吃早餐的时间更少了。 
 C)  他们比过去吃更多水果。 
 D)  他们在面包上涂果酱而不是黄油。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They spend less time eating breakfast. 
 【定位】 P2 The second reason they say is lifestyle changes in the country, with people dedicating less time to breakfast when bread would traditionally be eaten with butter and jam. 
 他们说的第二个原因是这个国家的生活方式发生了变化——人们花在早餐上的时间变少了，而早餐传统上是把面包配上黄油和果酱来吃的。 

 【信号】 明示 lifestyle changes 标题句 。The second reason they say is lifestyle changes in the country 直接以 lifestyle changes 标题切入，紧接的 dedicating less time to breakfast 就是这条生活方式变化的具体内容，是本题答案句的明确信号。 

 【替换】 dedicating less time to breakfast ↔ They spend less time eating breakfast. dedicate=spend 的同义替换 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 They bake more bread at home. 在录音里找不到 bake/at home 的踪迹，是无中生有的方向。 
 C) eat more fruit than they used to 用了 used to 这种生活方式变化的常见框架来伪装，但 fruit 在录音里完全没出现，属于借框架编内容。 
 D) 原词陷阱 录音里 bread would traditionally be eaten with butter and jam 表明的是传统上面包是'同时'配黄油和果酱来吃，并不存在'用果酱取代黄油'。选项 put jam instead of butter on bread 盗用了 butter 和 jam 两个原词，又添加 instead of 制造一个原文没有的替换关系。  借用原文：bread would traditionally be eaten with butter and jam

questions.prompt: When would the man like to leave for London?
options: After the rush hour.
Early in the morning.
As soon as possible.
Around lunch time.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 When would the man like to leave for London? 

 【翻译】 这位男士想什么时候出发去伦敦? 
 A)  高峰时段之后。 
 B)  一大早。 
 C)  越快越好。 
 D)  午餐时间前后。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） After the rush hour. 
 【定位】 P4 Well, after the rush hour, I think. We'd like to avoid the crowds if possible. So, probably sometime around 10 o'clock. 
 嗯，我想是早高峰之后吧。我们希望尽量避开人潮。所以大概十点钟左右。 

 【信号】 被问者的直接应答 。前一句售票员问 What time would you like to go?，紧接着男士开口 Well, after the rush hour, I think.——这是"问—答"结构里答的那一句，是听力定位答案最稳的信号。 

 【替换】 after the rush hour ↔ After the rush hour. 原句原词整体回收 
 avoid the crowds ↔ After the rush hour. 因果同义印证 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 录音里没有任何 early in the morning 的表述；恰恰相反，男士说 after the rush hour，明显是"避开早高峰"——选 B 等于把"早高峰之后"反着理解成"清早"。 
 C) 与原文相反 As soon as possible. 与男士 after the rush hour avoid the crowds 的意思相反——他要的是错开高峰、不是越早越好。  借用原文：after the rush hour 

 D) 过度推断 男士说 sometime around 10 o'clock，10 点不是午餐时间；选 D 是把"10 点"误推到 lunch time，属于对原词的过度引申。  借用原文：around 10 o'clock

questions.prompt: What is the man's other request?
options: Two first class seats.
Two seats together.
One window seat.
One seat near the exit.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the man's other request? 

 【翻译】 这位男士的另一个要求是什么? 
 A)  两个头等座位。 
 B)  两个相邻座位。 
 C)  一个靠窗座位。 
 D)  一个靠近出口的座位。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） One window seat. 
 【定位】 P8 Second class is fine. Thanks. Is there any chance we could have a window seat for one of those? 
 二等座就行，谢谢。其中一张能不能给我们安排一个靠窗的座位？ 

 【信号】 请求句 Is there any chance 。男士在确认席别后用 Is there any chance we could have a window seat for one of those? 主动提出一个"额外要求"，这种请求句式是答案信号；前半 Second class is fine. 是先答售票员问题，真正的 other request 在 chance 之后。 

 【替换】 a window seat for one of those ↔ One window seat. 数量+席位类型逐项对齐 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 男士明确说 Second class is fine.——选的是二等座，不是头等座；A 项盗用了对话里讨论过的 first class 话题词，但极性反了。  借用原文：Second class is fine. 

 B) 张冠李戴 I've booked those seats next to each other for you. 是售票员主动给出的服务，不是男士提出的请求；B 项盗用了 next to each other = together 的语义，但来源不是男士——属于把售票员的话安到男士头上。  借用原文：I've booked those seats next to each other for you. 

 D) 未提及 One seat near the exit. 里的 exit 在录音中完全没念，属于凭常识或对窗口座位的反义臆造出的干扰项。

questions.prompt: Where should the man wait for the train?
options: In the middle of the platform.
At the far end of the platform.
Behind the yellow line.
In the waiting room.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Where should the man wait for the train? 

 【翻译】 这位男士应该在哪里等火车? 
 A)  在站台中间。 
 B)  在站台最远端。 
 C)  在黄线后面。 
 D)  在候车室。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） At the far end of the platform. 
 【定位】 P11 All you need to do is wait at the far end of the platform. 
 你们要做的就是在站台的最远端等候。 

 【信号】 All you need to do 的指示句 。All you need to do is wait at the far end of the platform. 用 All you need to do 这种强调式的祈使指示句，等于给出一条明确指令，是答案信号；后面紧跟 When the train arrives, tell the train guard... 是补充流程，不是该等的地点。 

 【替换】 at the far end of the platform ↔ At the far end of the platform. 原句完整搬运 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音只说在 the far end of the platform 等车，没有说 middle；A 项盗用了原文里的 platform 一词，把方位偷换成 middle。  借用原文：at the far end of the platform 

 C) 未提及 录音里完全没提 yellow line；这是日常乘车经验里的安全规则，主体考生容易凭母语常识硬选。 
 D) 未提及 录音里也没提 waiting room；男士被告知直接到 the far end of the platform 等车，不是去候车室。

questions.prompt: What should the man do to collect the bicycles?
options: Wait in a queue for his turn.
Go to the baggage claim area.
Pay an extra fee for the service.
Give the ticket to the train guard.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What should the man do to collect the bicycles? 

 【翻译】 这位男士应该做什么来取自行车? 
 A)  排队等候轮到他。 
 B)  去行李提取区。 
 C)  为这项服务支付额外费用。 
 D)  把车票交给列车员。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Give the ticket to the train guard. 
 【定位】 P11 When you arrive in London, hand the ticket to the guard and he will return the bicycles to you. 
 等你们到了伦敦，把票交给乘务员，他会把自行车还给你们。 

 【信号】 When you arrive 的时间状语+祈使 。When you arrive in London, hand the ticket to the guard and he will return the bicycles to you. 这一句的 When you arrive in London 正好对应题干 to collect the bicycles 的"到达后"语境；hand the ticket 是祈使动词，他/还给你 是结果——这是地道的答案信号。 

 【替换】 hand the ticket to the guard ↔ Give the ticket to the train guard. 同义动词替换 
 he will return the bicycles to you ↔ Give the ticket to the train guard. 因果配套印证 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 录音里没有 wait in a queue 或类似的排队动作；A 项是凭常识"想象车站要排队"硬塞的。 
 B) 偷换概念 baggage claim area 是机场用语；录音里说的是 he will help you secure the bicycles in the last carriage——在火车最后一节车厢交接，不存在行李提取区。B 项盗用了与"取回"语义相似的航空场景词。  借用原文：he will help you secure the bicycles in the last carriage 

 C) 与原文相反 售票员明确说 It's no extra cost. The price will be the same.——不会再收额外费用；C 项却说要 pay an extra fee，与原文极性正相反。  借用原文：It's no extra cost.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about hat factories in Britain?
options: Almost all of them were operating at a deficit.
They have all been turned into movie theatres.
Nearly all of them closed down decades ago.
They have adapted to meet fashion changes.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about hat factories in Britain? 

 【翻译】 关于英国的帽子工厂，我们了解到什么？ 
 A)  它们几乎全都在亏损经营。 
 B)  它们全都已被改造成电影院。 
 C)  它们几乎全都在几十年前就关闭了。 
 D)  它们已经适应了时尚变化。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Nearly all of them closed down decades ago. 
 【定位】 P6 There used to be many hat factories in Britain until around the 1950s, but fashion changed and most people stopped wearing hats. So practically all of those factories had to close down. 
 英国曾经有很多帽厂，一直延续到 1950 年代左右；但后来潮流变了，大多数人不再戴帽子，所以那些工厂几乎全都倒闭了。 

 【信号】 but + So 的双重连接信号 。but fashion changed 的 but 把话题从「曾经繁荣」掰向「后来衰落」，紧接 So practically all of those factories had to close down. 的 So 又把因果一锤定音——「but 转折 + So 结论」这一组连贯信号，正是答案句的标志。 

 【替换】 practically all of those factories had to close down ↔ Nearly all of them closed down decades ago. practically ≈ nearly，1950s = decades ago 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 录音从头到尾没提帽厂亏损的事，Almost all of them were operating at a deficit. 是把「衰落」这个事实换成了「亏损」这个具体的财务原因，原文并未给出。 
 B) 原词陷阱 They have all been turned into movie theatres. 盗用了 we transformed it into a movie theater 中「改造成电影院」的措辞——但录音明说这件事只发生在「这一家」帽厂（This one, in particular, was closed for 47 years before we transformed it into a movie theater.），把单数案例扩大到全部，是典型张冠李戴。  借用原文：This one, in particular, was closed for 47 years before we transformed it into a movie theater. 

 D) 与原文相反 录音说 fashion changed and most people stopped wearing hats 才导致工厂关门——是被潮流「抛弃」，而非 They have adapted to meet fashion changes. 所说的「成功顺应潮流」，极性正好相反。  借用原文：fashion changed and most people stopped wearing hats

questions.prompt: What is special about Cube Movie Theater?
options: It shows foreign movies exclusively.
It shows movies from the 1950s.
It is the oldest theatre in London.
It is located next to a hat factory.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is special about Cube Movie Theater? 

 【翻译】 Cube电影院有什么特别之处？ 
 A)  它专门放映外国电影。 
 B)  它放映20世纪50年代的电影。 
 C)  它是伦敦最古老的电影院。 
 D)  它位于一家帽子工厂旁边。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It shows foreign movies exclusively. 
 【定位】 P8 We are the only movie theater in the whole country that only shows foreign movies. 
 我们是全国唯一一家只放外语电影的影院。 

 【信号】 the only + only 双重独家信号 。the only movie theater in the whole country 用 the only 给独特性钉了第一颗钉子，that only shows foreign movies 又用 only 把范围进一步缩死——「the only ... only」这种双重限定，是答案句最强的信号。 

 【替换】 only shows foreign movies ↔ It shows foreign movies exclusively. only ↔ exclusively 的同义替换 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 It shows movies from the 1950s. 把第 12 题里出现过的 until around the 1950s 这个时间数字盗过来当影院题材，制造「听到 1950s 就想选」的诱惑——可 1950s 在录音里讲的是「帽厂的年代」，而非影院上映的电影年代，是典型的张冠李戴。  借用原文：until around the 1950s 

 C) 未提及 It is the oldest theatre in London. 录音里压根没提「最老」，反而说 Cube Movie Theater has been around now for 11 years.——只有 11 年的影院显然算不上 oldest。  借用原文：Cube Movie Theater has been around now for 11 years. 

 D) 原词陷阱 It is located next to a hat factory. 利用了录音里 It's located in what used to be a hat factory. 的措辞——但原文说的是「影院开在原先的帽厂里」，next to（紧邻）与 in what used to be（开在旧址里）位置关系完全不同，是典型的偷换位置概念。  借用原文：It's located in what used to be a hat factory.

questions.prompt: What does the man say about most people in London?
options: They wear hats on social occasions.
They don't speak foreign languages.
They enjoy watching foreign movies.
They don't go to movie theatres often.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say about most people in London? 

 【翻译】 关于伦敦的大多数人，这位男士说了什么？ 
 A)  他们在社交场合戴帽子。 
 B)  他们不会说外语。 
 C)  他们喜欢看外国电影。 
 D)  他们不常去电影院。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They don't speak foreign languages. 
 【定位】 P9 Is there enough demand for that? I would have thought that in London, most people don't speak foreign languages. 
 这种电影真有那么多人看吗？我本以为伦敦的大多数人是不懂外语的。 

 【信号】 I would have thought + most people don't 的观点信号 。I would have thought that ... 是男方亮出自己看法的标志性结构，紧跟其后的 most people don't speak foreign languages 就是他对伦敦多数人的判断——「I thought / I would have thought」之后那句是观点句，必抓。 

 【替换】 most people don't speak foreign languages ↔ They don't speak foreign languages. 几乎原句对原句，主语等值替换 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 They wear hats on social occasions. 利用录音里反复出现的 most people stopped wearing hats 这个词组制造熟悉感——但原文是说英国人「不再戴帽」，并非「在社交场合戴帽」，且这句话是关于「英国人对帽子的态度」，不是「伦敦人对外语的态度」，话题与说话人都对不上。  借用原文：most people stopped wearing hats 

 C) 与原文相反 They enjoy watching foreign movies. 的极性正好和男方观点相反——男方明说 most people don't speak foreign languages，正是在质疑「demand 够不够」，而非肯定他们爱看外语片；而后女方才反驳说外语片仍有市场，但那是女方的话，不是男方的。  借用原文：most people don't speak foreign languages 

 D) 未提及 They don't go to movie theatres often. 是关于伦敦人「去影院频率」的描述，录音里从未提及伦敦人「常不常去影院」，属于无中生有。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about foreign movies shown in London?
options: They are meant mostly for immigrants.
They attract large crowds of young Londoners.
They are hard for English people to appreciate.
They have an English translation on the screen.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about foreign movies shown in London? 

 【翻译】 关于在伦敦放映的外国电影，这位女士说了什么？ 
 A)  它们主要是为移民准备的。 
 B)  它们吸引大批年轻的伦敦人。 
 C)  它们对英国人来说很难欣赏。 
 D)  它们在屏幕上有英文翻译。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They have an English translation on the screen. 
 【定位】 P10 Furthermore, I might add, all movies come with English text at the bottom of the screen. So even if you don't understand what the actors say, you can still read it. 
 另外我得补一句，所有的电影都在屏幕下方配有英文文字，所以哪怕听不懂演员说什么，你也能读字幕。 

 【信号】 Furthermore + I might add 的补充强调信号 。女方一连用 Furthermore 和 I might add 两个补充强调标志把这条信息推到台前，紧跟其后给出「屏幕下方有英文」这一具体事实——「Furthermore + I might add」组合是答主特别想让人记住的那一句的信号灯。 

 【替换】 all movies come with English text at the bottom of the screen ↔ They have an English translation on the screen. English text ↔ English translation；at the bottom of the screen ↔ on the screen 
 even if you don't understand what the actors say, you can still read it ↔ They have an English translation on the screen. 补充句佐证字幕功能 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 They are meant mostly for immigrants. 把外语片的受众限定为「移民」，录音里完全没出现 immigrants 这个话题，是凭常识脑补出来的无中生有。 
 B) 原词陷阱 They attract large crowds of young Londoners. 利用了录音中 lots of people interested in watching such movies 与 London 的搭配——但原文只说「有很多人感兴趣」，并未限定为「年轻伦敦人」；选项把宽泛的 lots of people 偷换成具体的 young Londoners，加了原文没有的修饰语 young。  借用原文：lots of people interested in watching such movies 

 C) 与原文相反 They are hard for English people to appreciate. 的极性和女方观点相反——女方一直在反驳「外语片在伦敦没人看」的怀疑，强调 there's enough demand 和 lots of people interested，没有任何「难以欣赏」的意思。  借用原文：there's enough demand

questions.prompt: What do we learn about Astrid Natley, a secondary school math teacher?
options: She doesn't think smartphones can replace tablets.
She incorporates smartphones into her teaching.
She cannot stop children using smartphones.
She regards smartphones as a distraction.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about Astrid Natley, a secondary school math teacher? 

 【翻译】 关于中学数学教师Astrid Natley，我们了解到什么？ 
 A)  她认为智能手机无法替代平板电脑。 
 B)  她将智能手机融入她的教学中。 
 C)  她无法阻止孩子们使用智能手机。 
 D)  她认为智能手机会分散注意力。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） She incorporates smartphones into her teaching. 
 【定位】 P3 Astrid Natley, a secondary school math teacher, incorporates phones into her classroom. 
 Astrid Natley是一位中学数学老师，她把手机融入到了自己的课堂里。 

 【信号】 人物登场首句即定调 。原文Astrid Natley, a secondary school math teacher, incorporates phones into her classroom.是该人物在文中首次出现的那句话，篇章独白介绍人物时通常"姓名+身份+核心做法"一句话点题，这种"登场首句"就是关于该人物事实的答案信号。 

 【替换】 incorporates phones into her classroom ↔ incorporates smartphones into her teaching phones=smartphones、classroom≈teaching 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音里她说My school doesn't have money for tablets，意思是"学校没钱买平板，所以才用手机"，盗用了原文的tablets一词，做成"她不认为手机能替代平板"这种相反观点，属于原词陷阱+与原文相反。  借用原文：My school doesn't have money for tablets 

 C) 偷换概念 录音If we stop children using phones, we're rejecting something they care about.是"如果我们阻止孩子用手机，等于拒绝他们在乎的东西"——是"不愿阻止"的价值判断；选项She cannot stop children using smartphones.盗用stop children using phones原词，却换成"无法阻止"，偷换了情态。  借用原文：If we stop children using phones, we're rejecting something they care about. 

 D) 与原文相反 原文她把手机视为a powerful tool in their hands，是正面评价；选项She regards smartphones as a distraction.却说她把手机视为"干扰"，立场与原文相反。  借用原文：a powerful tool in their hands

questions.prompt: Why does Helen Lockhart, a registered nurse, support a complete ban on smartphone use in the classroom?
options: To enforce school discipline.
To make students concentrate.
To help children grow up to be professionals.
To cultivate children's good study habits.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does Helen Lockhart, a registered nurse, support a complete ban on smartphone use in the classroom? 

 【翻译】 注册护士Helen Lockhart为什么支持在课堂上完全禁止使用智能手机？ 
 A)  为了执行学校纪律。 
 B)  为了让学生集中注意力。 
 C)  为了帮助孩子们成长为专业人士。 
 D)  为了培养孩子们良好的学习习惯。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） To help children grow up to be professionals. 
 【定位】 P4 We need to teach children how to behave like the professionals they are striving to become. 
 我们需要教孩子们像他们将来要努力成为的那些专业人士一样去行事。 

 【信号】 段尾"need to"目的陈述 。原文We need to teach children how to behave like the professionals they are striving to become.位于Helen段落末尾，以We need to开头的句子是她整段论证的结论与目的——"need to"是表目的的强信号词，是答案信号。 

 【替换】 teach children how to behave like the professionals they are striving to become ↔ To help children grow up to be professionals behave like professionals=grow up to be professionals 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音I will be subject to disciplinary procedure是她讲自己工作场所的纪律后果，作为引出"教孩子像专业人士"目的的铺垫；选项To enforce school discipline.盗用disciplinary原词，扭成"她支持禁手机的目的是维护校纪"，张冠李戴。  借用原文：I will be subject to disciplinary procedure 

 B) 未提及 录音里Helen段没有任何关于concentration/focus/attention的表述，选项To make students concentrate.是听上去合理但原文未提及的干扰项。 
 D) 未提及 录音里Helen段没有提到study habits或类似的"养成学习习惯"，选项To cultivate children's good study habits.是另一个"听上去禁手机的合理理由"，属于未提及陷阱。

questions.prompt: What should students do in the classroom according to Richard Stone, an English teacher?
options: Use books and pens only.
Cut down their screen time.
Make full use of electronic devices.
Learn to use the internet for research.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What should students do in the classroom according to Richard Stone, an English teacher? 

 【翻译】 根据英语教师Richard Stone的说法，学生在课堂上应该做什么？ 
 A)  只使用书本和笔。 
 B)  减少他们的屏幕使用时间。 
 C)  充分利用电子设备。 
 D)  学习使用互联网进行研究。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Use books and pens only. 
 【定位】 P5 so let's leave phones and laptops at home, and show them a different world in their lessons—one of books and pens 
 所以让我们把手机和笔记本电脑都留在家里，在课堂上向他们展示一个不一样的世界——一个由书本和钢笔构成的世界。 

 【信号】 let's+破折号定义结论句 。原文so let's leave phones and laptops at home, and show them a different world in their lessons—one of books and pens以"so let's…"建议式结构开头，又用破折号引出对"a different world"的同位语解释"one of books and pens"——这是典型的"结论+具象化"信号，是答案句。 

 【替换】 leave phones and laptops at home ↔ Use books and pens only 把手机和电脑留家=不用电子设备 
 show them a different world in their lessons—one of books and pens ↔ Use books and pens only books and pens的世界=只用书本和钢笔 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 录音Children are getting more than enough screen time in their lives without the need to bring their phone into the classroom.提到screen time，是Richard用以解释"为什么不该带手机进课堂"的背景论据，并非他对学生课堂行为的主张；选项Cut down their screen time.盗用screen time原词来制造听到就想选的诱惑。  借用原文：Children are getting more than enough screen time in their lives without the need to bring their phone into the classroom. 

 C) 与原文相反 Richard明确主张let's leave phones and laptops at home，是反对在课堂用电子设备；选项Make full use of electronic devices.反过来说"充分利用电子设备"，立场反向。  借用原文：let's leave phones and laptops at home 

 D) 与原文相反 录音The internet is too easy and too unreliable a research tool里，Richard明明在批评"互联网作为研究工具太简单、太不可靠"；选项Learn to use the internet for research.盗用internet、research原词，反过来说"学会用网做研究"，立场翻转。  借用原文：The internet is too easy and too unreliable a research tool

questions.prompt: How did Kate earn the reward from her mother?
options: By cleaning the kitchen floor.
By looking after her baby brother.
By helping her mother do the dishes.
By helping her brother wash windows.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How did Kate earn the reward from her mother? 

 【翻译】 Kate 是如何从她母亲那里获得奖励的? 
 A)  通过清洁厨房地板。 
 B)  通过照顾她的小弟弟。 
 C)  通过帮助她母亲洗碗。 
 D)  通过帮助她弟弟擦窗户。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） By helping her brother wash windows. 
 【定位】 P1 Kate, a six-year-old girl, helped her brother wash windows to get a reward promised by her mother, a purple doll that she wanted. 
 凯特，一个六岁的小女孩，帮哥哥擦窗户，为的是拿到妈妈答应的奖励——一只她想要的紫色娃娃。 

 【信号】 to get a reward 的目的状语 。helped her brother wash windows to get a reward promised by her mother 这句里 to get a reward 是目的状语，前面的动作（helped her brother wash windows）就是为了拿奖励而做的事，正是题目问的 how earn the reward。 

 【替换】 helped her brother wash windows ↔ helping her brother wash windows 几乎原词复现，仅时态变形 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 By cleaning the kitchen floor. 是常见家务但录音里完全没提，属于未提及型干扰，专骗那些把做家务挣奖励脑补成打扫卫生的考生。 
 B) 原词陷阱 By looking after her baby brother. 盗用了录音里的 brother 一词制造熟感，但录音里说的是 helped her brother wash windows，是凯特帮哥哥，而不是照看弟弟。  借用原文：helped her brother wash windows 

 C) 原词陷阱 By helping her mother do the dishes. 蹭了录音里 helped 与为妈妈做事的氛围，但录音里凯特帮的是 brother、做的是 wash windows，不是帮 mother do the dishes。  借用原文：promised by her mother

questions.prompt: What did Kate do after her mother left the room?
options: She ordered a large number of dolls.
She checked if a purple doll was ordered.
She mistakenly canceled her mom's order.
She ordered a more expensive doll instead.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did Kate do after her mother left the room? 

 【翻译】 Kate 的母亲离开房间后她做了什么? 
 A)  她订购了大量娃娃。 
 B)  她查看是否订购了紫色娃娃。 
 C)  她错误地取消了她妈妈的订单。 
 D)  她订购了一个更贵的娃娃。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） She ordered a large number of dolls. 
 【定位】 P1 15 minutes and a few clicks later, with more than $350 worth of dolls in her cart, Kate placed the order and ran off to play. 
 15 分钟和几次点击之后，购物车里装着价值 350 多美元的娃娃，凯特下了单，跑去玩了。 

 【信号】 总结性结尾句加数量爆炸 。15 minutes and a few clicks later, with more than $350 worth of dolls in her cart, Kate placed the order 这句是这一段动作的收束句，350 美元、placed the order 几个反常细节直接交代了凯特在妈妈走后做了什么——她下了一大堆娃娃的订单。这种数量或价格爆表的细节，几乎一定是答案信号。 

 【替换】 more than $350 worth of dolls in her cart ↔ She ordered a large number of dolls. 数量上的同义改写 
 Kate placed the order ↔ She ordered a large number of dolls. 动词短语到单动词的等值替换 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 She checked if a purple doll was ordered. 盗用了录音里 purple doll 和 check the shipping status 制造她检查了紫娃娃订单的幻觉，但录音里 check 的是 shipping status（物流），而且那是动作的起点不是后果，她做了什么的真正答案是后面的下单。  借用原文：Kate asked if she could check the shipping status 

 C) 张冠李戴 She mistakenly canceled her mom's order. 录音里恰恰是 cancel 这个词出现了，但执行者是妈妈第二天才取消的两单，不是凯特；凯特做的事是反方向的加单。  借用原文：She was able to cancel two of them 

 D) 偷换概念 She ordered a more expensive doll instead. 录音里凯特的问题不是换了一只更贵的，而是在原本一只之外又加了一大堆，重点是数量爆炸而不是单只价格升级，是过度推断式的偏移。  借用原文：more than $350 worth of dolls in her cart

questions.prompt: What did Kate's family do after the packages arrived?
options: They asked the children's hospital to pick them.
They took all of them to the children's hospital.
They opened all of them one by one.
They discussed where to keep them.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did Kate's family do after the packages arrived? 

 【翻译】 包裹到达后 Kate 一家做了什么? 
 A)  他们请儿童医院来取这些包裹。 
 B)  他们把所有包裹带到了儿童医院。 
 C)  他们逐一打开了所有包裹。 
 D)  他们讨论了把这些包裹放在哪里。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） They took all of them to the children's hospital. 
 【定位】 P2 Instead of sending back the dolls, her father suggested giving them to the local children's hospital. So the next week, Kate's family loaded up their car and took all the dolls to the playroom at the children's hospital. 
 她父亲提议不要把娃娃寄回去，而是捐给当地的儿童医院。于是第二周，凯特一家装了一车，把所有娃娃送到了儿童医院的活动室。 

 【信号】 结果句 So 加 took all the dolls 。So the next week, Kate's family loaded up their car and took all the dolls to the playroom at the children's hospital. 中的 So 是因果结果信号，把前面父亲提议的话变成实际行动，直接给出全家把所有娃娃送去了医院这个确定答案。 

 【替换】 took all the dolls to the playroom at the children's hospital ↔ They took all of them to the children's hospital. 几乎原句直译 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 They asked the children's hospital to pick them. 蹭了录音里的 children's hospital 制造熟感，但录音里是家里人把娃娃送去，不是请医院来挑，动作方向完全相反。  借用原文：took all the dolls to the playroom at the children's hospital 

 C) 张冠李戴 They opened all of them one by one. 盗用了录音里 opened up all the boxes 这个动作，但执行人是凯特和医院里的小女孩患者们，不是凯特一家，而且发生地点也在医院里、不是包裹一到家就打开。  借用原文：they opened up all the boxes together 

 D) 未提及 discussed where to keep them. 这个动作完全没出现，录音直奔父亲提议捐医院，没经过商量放哪儿。

questions.prompt: According to recent research conducted in Australia, what has a lasting impact on one's life?
options: The time one starts school.
The classroom atmosphere.
The school that one attends.
The relationship with classmates.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 According to recent research conducted in Australia, what has a lasting impact on one's life? 

 【翻译】 根据最近在澳大利亚进行的研究,什么对一个人的一生有持久影响? 
 A)  一个人开始上学的时间。 
 B)  课堂氛围。 
 C)  一个人就读的学校。 
 D)  与同学的关系。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） The time one starts school. 
 【定位】 P1 The researchers found that the time when a person starts school has an enduring impact on their lives. 
 研究者发现，一个人开始上学的时间会对其一生产生持久的影响。 

 【信号】 researchers found 这一研究结论信号 。篇章独白里 The researchers found that 是典型的结论提示词——后面紧跟的句子就是研究的核心发现，几乎必然是答案句。再加上 has an enduring impact on their lives 与题干 lasting impact on one's life 完全对应，可以确认就是这一句。 

 【替换】 the time when a person starts school ↔ The time one starts school. 句式压缩同义替换 
 has an enduring impact on their lives ↔ a lasting impact on one's life 形容词同义替换 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 录音从头到尾没有出现 atmosphere、classroom environment 这类表达，The classroom atmosphere. 属于教育话题里常用的凑数干扰，没有任何原文支撑。 
 C) 原词陷阱 The school that one attends. 借了录音里反复出现的 school 一词来制造熟悉感，但录音说的是 the time when a person starts school——重点在 time 不在 school 本身，把入学时间偷换成了上的什么学校，是典型的原词陷阱。  借用原文：the time when a person starts school 

 D) 原词陷阱 The relationship with classmates. 提到的 classmates 虽然在录音里以 compared to their classmates 出现过一次，但录音只是用 classmates 来做参照对象，没有讨论同学关系本身对人生的影响，属于借词不传义。  借用原文：compared to their classmates

questions.prompt: What was the purpose of the Australian research?
options: To help parents decide when to send their children to school.
To find causes for differences in the participants' performance.
To identify students having potential to be professional athletes.
To offer constructive suggestions for making educational policies.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What was the purpose of the Australian research? 

 【翻译】 澳大利亚这项研究的目的是什么? 
 A)  帮助家长决定何时送孩子上学。 
 B)  找出参与者表现差异的原因。 
 C)  识别有潜力成为职业运动员的学生。 
 D)  为制定教育政策提供建设性建议。 

 【答案】 B （目的题） To find causes for differences in the participants' performance. 
 【定位】 P1 But the Australian researchers wanted to discover what was driving these differences. 
 但澳大利亚的研究者们想要弄清楚究竟是什么在驱动这些差异。 

 【信号】 but + wanted to discover 这一双重信号 。But the Australian researchers wanted to discover what was driving these differences. 既有转折信号 but，又有目的结构 wanted to discover，两个信号叠加，几乎可以确认这就是研究目的的官方表述句。 

 【替换】 wanted to discover what was driving these differences ↔ To find causes for differences in the participants' performance. 同义动词与名词改写 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 To help parents decide when to send their children to school. 借了 starts school 的话题词，把研究目的偷换成给家长的择校建议，但录音从未提及 parents 或 advice，是典型的应用层偷换。  借用原文：the time when a person starts school 

 C) 原词陷阱 To identify students having potential to be professional athletes. 借了录音里 professional athletes 一词来制造听到就想选的诱惑，但录音里 athletes 只是顺带列举的成功人士之一，不是研究目的。  借用原文：professional athletes 

 D) 过度推断 To offer constructive suggestions for making educational policies. 把研究目的拔高到教育政策层面，录音里完全没有出现 policy、policymaker 或 suggestion 等表达，属于无中生有。

questions.prompt: Who were the participants in the researchers' first study?
options: Political leaders.
Financial analysts.
Professional athletes.
High-school students.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Who were the participants in the researchers' first study? 

 【翻译】 研究人员第一项研究的参与者是谁? 
 A)  政治领袖。 
 B)  金融分析师。 
 C)  职业运动员。 
 D)  高中生。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） High-school students. 
 【定位】 P2 In the first study more than 600 high school students were surveyed about their tendency to take risks and feel confident. 
 在第一项研究中，超过六百名高中生接受了关于其冒险倾向与自信感的调查。 

 【信号】 In the first study 这一段落标志 。In the first study 是典型的研究步骤标志词，后面紧跟的就是该研究的被试群体，是非常明确的定位信号；紧随其后的 high school students 就是答案。 

 【替换】 more than 600 high school students ↔ High-school students. 数量修饰被剥离的概括式替换 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Political leaders. 借了录音末尾 political leaders 一词制造熟悉感，但 political leaders 是在 including athletes, political leaders and entrepreneurs 这一举例结构里出现，是成功人士的例子，不是第一项研究的被试。  借用原文：including athletes, political leaders and entrepreneurs 

 B) 未提及 Financial analysts. 在录音里完全没有对应表达，录音只在 managing their finances 中出现过 finances 一词，但讲的是受试者管理财务时的冒险行为，与金融分析师这个职业身份毫不相关。 
 C) 原词陷阱 Professional athletes. 借了录音里反复出现的 professional athletes 一词，但录音里 athletes 始终是作为成功人士的例子出现，从未被列为第一项研究的被试群体，属于借词换位。  借用原文：professional athletes

questions.prompt: According to the researchers, what is one characteristic of successful people?
options: Leadership ability.
Commitment to work.
Risk-taking.
Self-confidence.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 According to the researchers, what is one characteristic of successful people? 

 【翻译】 根据研究人员的说法,成功人士的一个特征是什么? 
 A)  领导能力。 
 B)  对工作的投入。 
 C)  冒险精神。 
 D)  自信。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Risk-taking. 
 【定位】 P2 While risk-taking can be considered a negative attribute, it's also a characteristic of successful people, including athletes, political leaders and entrepreneurs. 
 尽管冒险有时被视为一种负面特质，但它同时也是成功人士的一种特征，包括运动员、政界领袖与企业家在内。 

 【信号】 while 让步 + it's also 转折强调 。While risk-taking can be considered a negative attribute, it's also a characteristic of successful people 用 while 引导让步、随后 it's also 强调真正想说的一面——这种让步+强调结构里的强调句几乎必然是答案。 

 【替换】 it's also a characteristic of successful people ↔ one characteristic of successful people 句式结构高度复现 
 risk-taking ↔ Risk-taking. 代词指代回填 

 【排除】 A) 过度推断 Leadership ability. 利用了录音末尾 political leaders 一词制造领导力联想，但录音说成功人士包括政界领袖，并没有把 leadership ability 列为他们的共性特征。  借用原文：including athletes, political leaders and entrepreneurs 

 B) 未提及 Commitment to work. 是非常常见的成功学描述，但录音里完全没有出现 commitment、dedication、hard work 等字眼，属于无中生有。 
 D) 原词陷阱 Self-confidence. 借了录音里多次出现的 self-confidence 与 feel confident，但录音只把 self-confidence 作为研究的假设变量，最终结论强调的特征是 risk-taking，不是 self-confidence。  借用原文：it's also a characteristic of successful people
